title: Théorie de Kumer ? + note Alexandre (bi tenseur…) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: pages 9-11 of this folder deal with Grothendieck's theory of maps (cartes). Page 9 treats the cartographic groups Γ_{p,q} (including Γ_{∞,3}, Γ_{∞,∞} and PSL(2,Z)), the regular maps C_{pq} and their quotients. Page 11 treats Schreier's index formula for free groups, π_1 of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, and the Galois-category description Ens(π) → C. This page gives the purely TOPOLOGICAL definition of a map, to be matched later with the combinatorial one (sets with an action of σ0, σ1, σ2).

Definition ('carte trouée', holed map). A pair (X ⊃ K), where X is a topological surface and K ⊂ X is a closed subspace of dimension 1. The condition is that every connected component of the cut-open surface Déc(X,K) (the 'découpe' of X along K) is homeomorphic to a 'standard hole' D_n^*, for some 1 ≤ n ≤ +∞.

The standard hole. Π_n is a combinatorial polygon of order n with vertices S_n, edges A_n and a third datum (F_n or R_n). |Π_n| is its realization: a circle subdivided into n arcs, or for n = ∞ a line subdivided at countably many points. This is the '… —•—•—• …' figure. One forms the cone-minus-apex |Π_n| × ]0,1], containing |Π_n| (presumably as the level 1, the boundary) and hence S_n. Then
D_n^* = |Π_n| × ]0,1] \ S_n.
So D_n^* is a once-punctured disc (the face centre is removed, hence 'trouée') whose boundary circle carries n marked points that are deleted. For n = ∞ it is a half-strip or half-plane whose boundary line has its vertex points removed. This is the face model of an infinite-valency face, matching Γ_{p,∞} and Γ_{∞,∞} from the previous page.

Figures.
- A pentagon coned from its centre: the face as a cone over its boundary polygon.
- Arcs with transverse arrows: the two sides of a cut edge.
- A circle with a tangent line and '±1/n': apparently an explicit model of the hole and its rotational symmetry of order n, perhaps the conformal or metric normalisation near the boundary.
- A circle with thickened arcs and a rotation arrow: rotation of the hole, i.e. the action of σ-generators on flags.
- σ0, σ1, σ2 with σ0, σ1 bracketed: the cartographic generators.
- At the bottom: a dual-graph-like picture with circled vertices and a circled face centre, i.e. star neighbourhoods of vertices and face centres.

The boxed Déc(X̂, ∞) and 'X̃ \ F' suggest the plan. Compactify by adding the face centres (and/or points at infinity) to get X̂, then cut. Alternatively, pass to the universal or regular cover X̃ minus the face centres F, to compare with C_{pq} and Γ_{pq} as on the previous page.

Purpose: to establish the equivalence between topological maps (possibly infinite, with face centres punctured) and transitive sets with an action of the cartographic group. This is the foundation for dessins d'enfants and Galois action as in the Esquisse.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The definition is only sketched, and two things are left implicit. First, which level of |Π_n| × ]0,1] contains S_n (it must be level 1, the boundary, for D_n^* to be the intended punctured disc with marked boundary). Second, how Déc(X,K) is defined at the vertices of K, i.e. points of K where it is not locally a 1-manifold; this is presumably why S_n is removed. Local finiteness conditions on K are not stated.

ideas.what: Topological definition of a map as (surface X, closed 1-dimensional K) such that the components of the cut surface are standard punctured polygonal discs
ideas.modern_name: topological map / cellular embedding of a graph; 'carte cellulaire'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Tutte, Jones–Singerman 1978). In Grothendieck's school: Malgoire–Voisin, 'Cartes cellulaires' (Montpellier, 1977)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of cartes and the cartographic group (in outline only)

ideas.what: 'Découpe' Déc(X,K): cutting a surface along a closed 1-dimensional subspace
ideas.modern_name: cutting a surface along a graph

ideas.what: Standard hole D_n^* allowing n = ∞ (faces of infinite valency, boundary a line), matching cartographic groups Γ_{p,∞} and Γ_{∞,∞}
ideas.modern_name: maps with infinite-valency faces; infinite maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jones–Singerman (1978) treat infinite valencies; Grothendieck in the Esquisse mentions Γ_{∞,∞}
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (cartographic groups with infinite indices)

ideas.what: Cartographic generators σ0, σ1, σ2 acting on flags, illustrated by rotations of the hole
ideas.modern_name: cartographic group / monodromy group of a map

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard topological definition of (possibly infinite) maps, with punctured faces modelled on cones over polygons. It fits the known Grothendieck/Malgoire–Voisin 'cartes cellulaires' and 'découpe' framework and the Esquisse. Nothing beyond a sketch of foundations is visible.
transcription_corrections: 'dits que troué standard' should read 'dits trous standard'.
The first displayed interval is ']0,1]' (half-open), the same as in the definition of D_n^*.
The third component of Π_n looks like 'R_n' (or an F written oddly) in the image, i.e. Π_n = (S_n, A_n, R_n). It is probably faces/flags data.
'pol. comb. ép.' is likely 'polyg. comb. épointé' or similar, i.e. 'combinatorial polygon of order n'. This reading is uncertain.
